citeAs: Krizhevsky, A. (2009). Learning Multiple Layers of Features from Tiny Images.
creator: Alex Krizhevsky
description: The CIFAR-100 dataset consists of 600 examples of each of 100 non-overlapping classes. It is a labeled subset of the 80 million tiny images dataset.
name: CIFAR-100
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors personally verified every label submitted by the labelers.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Labelers were given a class and asked to examine images found with that class as the search term. They were instructed to reject images which did not belong to their assigned class based on criteria such as photo-realism and having one prominent instance. The authors personally verified every label submitted.
rai:dataCollection: Paid students labeled a subset of the 80 million tiny images dataset (which was originally collected from the web using WordNet nouns) by filtering out mislabeled images.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of 80 million colour images downscaled to 32x32 and spread out across 79000 search terms, collected from the web using WordNet nouns.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate images were removed from the dataset by comparing images with the L2 norm. The dataset was then divided into a training and test set.
